entradas.text: Dark clouds were looming over Deyr. They looked daunting as our convoy started approaching the century-old cemetery.
“Anton.”
“Sir, we have arrived.”
“Mr. President.”
It looked like it was going to rain. Certainly fitting weather for a funeral.
As expected, Bernard Circas's passing maintained its media traction and all of Sordland was paying attention to the ceremony. Especially to what I would say in my speech today.
Rain drops were running down the car window when Serge opened my door and held an umbrella over my head. As soon as I got out, flashes from the cameras blinded me.
“It's okay Serge. I will hold my own umbrella.”
entradas.menu: “It's okay Serge. I will hold my own umbrella.”

entradas.text: “Thank you.”
entradas.menu: “Thank you.”

entradas.text: “As you wish sir.”
“It's my duty, sir.”
He handed me the umbrella and started waiting next to the car with his own.
He silently started following me while holding the umbrella.
Petr and Karl exited from their own cars in the convoy. They made their way over to me.
“I just wanted to inform you that the perimeter is clear and secured completely. There is no one getting in or out without our knowledge.”
“We don't want something similar happening again, do we?”
entradas.menu: “We don't want something similar happening again, do we?”

entradas.text: “You better be right for your sake.”
entradas.menu: “You better be right for your sake.”

entradas.text: “Good work. Thank you Karl.”
entradas.menu: “Good work. Thank you Karl.”

entradas.text: “I have taken the necessary precautions. I personally made sure of that. We are all safe.”
“Absolutely not, Mr. President. The same mistakes will never happen again. I personally made sure of that.”
Karl bowed his head with respect.
“Good. If anything happens to Anton, you will have to answer to the First Lady.”
“And trust me Karl. You don't want that.”
Petr let out a laugh, which drew some attention from bereaved attendees.
“Petr, you are being inconsiderate.”
entradas.menu: “Petr, you are being inconsiderate.”

entradas.text: “I don't think any of us want that.”
entradas.menu: “I don't think any of us want that.”

entradas.text: I gestured at Petr to lower his voice a bit.
entradas.menu: Gesture Petr to lower his voice.

entradas.text: “You are right. Sorry.”
“You are right. Sorry.”
“Indeed.”
It started to rain. Several unintelligible voices were heard from Karl's radio. He stepped out to reply and returned shortly.
“We have a small problem, sir.”
“A few -- five to be exact -- Red Youth members are here to attend the funeral. They apparently said they wish to pay their respects to their fallen comrade.”
“Should we let them in?”
“Let them in.”
entradas.menu: “Let them in.”

entradas.text: “Absolutely not, it is too risky.”
entradas.menu: “Absolutely not.”

entradas.text: “Do you think they pose a security threat?”
entradas.menu: “Do you think they pose a security threat?”

entradas.text: “No. They were thoroughly searched. It looks like they really are here to attend the funeral.”
“As you command.”
“Let's head over. They are about to start.”
We walked towards the crowd circled around the grave. Everyone in attendance was wearing black in mourning. The rain started pouring heavily.
“Let them in but put a few guards on them to be safe.”
entradas.menu: “Let them in but put a few guards on them.”

entradas.text: Bernard's widow and daughter were in the front row, staring at the coffin with a mixture of disbelief, confusion and above all, a cold, unforgiving sadness.
Before taking my place to observe the ceremony, I gave my condolences to Bernard's wife and his daughter who looked at me. She reminded me of Deana.
Both of their eyes were very red and swollen from weeping.
When the religious ceremony was done, I was invited by the priest to deliver my speech. I took the podium. I felt like I had a lump in my throat. I couldn't get the daughter's eyes out of my head.
“Today, we are mourning Bernard Circas, a father, a husband and a loyal servant of this country.”
entradas.menu: “Today, we are mourning Bernard Circas, a father, a husband and a loyal servant of this country.”

entradas.text: Towards the back of the crowd, I spotted the members of the Red Youth, wearing red shirts and black bands of mourning on their arms. They seemed ruly and were respectfully bowing their heads.
There was complete silence except for the sound of raindrops.
“Regardless of his ideology, this was a heinous act made towards a good man. We must end this cycle of violence now.”
entradas.menu: “Regardless of his ideology, this was a heinous act made towards a good man. We must end this cycle of violence.”

entradas.text: “I interpret this attack as an attack against Sordland and by extension, against me personally.”
entradas.menu: “I interpret this attack as an attack against Sordland and by extension, against me personally.”

entradas.text: “We will make sure that unfortunate events such as this will never happen ever again.”
entradas.menu: “We will make sure that unfortunate events such as this will never happen again.”

entradas.text: “He was a true comrade and he fought for what he believed in, his ideal vision of Sordland, in every step of his life. We must learn from him.”
entradas.menu: “He was a true comrade and he fought for what he believed in, his ideal vision of Sordland, in every step of his life.”

entradas.text: “A moment of silence please.”
entradas.menu: “A moment of silence please.”

entradas.text: “Thank you.”
entradas.menu: “Thank you.”

entradas.text: “I would now like to recite a part from one of the poems he left us.”
entradas.menu: “I would now like to recite one of the poems he left us.”

entradas.text: “Our only strength is the will to survive, knowing that we will perish, knowing nothing more absolute.”
entradas.menu: “Our only strength is the will to survive, knowing that we will perish, knowing nothing more absolute.”

entradas.text: “I promise you this. The blood of Bernard will not remain on the sacred ground of Sordland.”
entradas.menu: “I promise you this. The blood of Bernard will not remain on the sacred ground of Sordland.”

entradas.text: During the silence, all that was heard were the ravens.
Some attendees started clapping, some crying.
The coffin was lowered into the grave by the gravekeepers. After a couple of minutes, Bernard Circas was with the soil, no more.
The widow thanked me with a soft and defeated voice before we dispersed.

On my way back to the car, I still couldn't get the eyes of Bernard's daughter, nor the faltering voice of his wife, out of my head. Would Deana, Monica and Franc look the same way if something happened to me?
Petr put his hand on my shoulder.
“That was a good speech.”
“Come on, it's time to go.”
“We've got work to do.”
I sensed only respect in his voice.
He was right. We had work to do. So much more to do.
“Thank you. I mean it.”
entradas.menu: “Thank you. I mean it.”

entradas.text: “I know you do.”
I realized that the rain had stopped, and I looked up.
The black clouds slowly dispersed and sunbeams enlightened our surroundings.
“This is a great loss for all of us, for our country.”
entradas.menu: “This is a great loss for all of us.”

entradas.text: “As we bid farewell to Bernard, I want to close with the words every Sord lives by: A Morgna wes core!”
entradas.menu: “As we bid farewell to Bernard, I want to close with the words every Sord lives by: A Morgna wes core!”

entradas.text: I stepped down from the podium. It was time to leave.
entradas.menu: Step down from the podium.

entradas.text: Everyone replied: “Vectern sis da!”. Victory is close.
With applauses, I stepped down from the podium. It was time to leave.
As someone once said: 'Even the darkest night will end and the sun will rise.'
I nodded.
entradas.menu: Nod.

entradas.text: “The tears of the family he left behind have a price that needs to be paid. I will not stop until it is paid in full.”
entradas.menu: “The tears of the family he left behind have a price that needs to be paid. I will not stop until it is paid in full.”

entradas.text: “Let us all mourn the passing of Bernard Circas and remember him well.”
entradas.menu: “Let us all mourn the passing of Bernard Circas and remember him well.”

entradas.text: “But, hatred begets hatred. There is only one way to overcome this vicious cycle. We must unite against the evil of this world.”
entradas.menu: “But, hatred begets hatred. There is only one way to overcome this vicious cycle. We must unite against the evil of this world.”

entradas.text: “It's time to go.”
entradas.menu: “It's time to go.”

entradas.text: “Agreed.”
“Hah! Right? I mean, life is full of tragedy. We should try to take it easy if we can.”
“You are the only one that can make me laugh at a funeral.”
entradas.menu: “You are the only one who can make me laugh at a funeral.”

entradas.text: “I will confess that I disagreed with Bernard Circas almost entirely. But it doesn't mean that he deserved this. Our country can be a better place.”
entradas.menu: “I will confess that I disagreed with Bernard Circas almost entirely. But it doesn't mean that he deserved this. Our country can be a better place.”

entradas.text: “Circas had a dream of a unified Sordland. In these next months we need to fulfill his dream and band together.”
entradas.menu: “Circas had a dream of a unified Sordland. In these next months we need to fulfill his dream and band together.”

entradas.text: Hope was still on the horizon.
“We rise, toward the sun! Those who died, died fighting. They are now buried in the sun. No need to mourn, there is a raid to the sun."
entradas.menu: “We rise, toward the sun! Those who died, died fighting. They are now buried in the sun. No need to mourn, there is a raid to the sun."

entradas.text: "They did not let us sing our songs. They are afraid, afraid of the dawn. They are afraid of hope, but our songs will be sung."
entradas.menu: "They did not let us sing our songs. They are afraid, afraid of the dawn. They are afraid of hope, but our songs will be sung."
